  // Restore the saved color scheme preference, or
  // enact the browser preference if "automatic", 
  // without expecting DOM load to have completed.
  //
  // Also restore any saved readingmode and ToC display preferences.
  function initializeReadingPreferences() {
    let saved_theme = localStorage.getItem("ar5iv_theme") || "automatic";
    if (saved_theme === "automatic") {
      if (window.matchMedia("(prefers-color-scheme: dark)").matches) {
        saved_theme = "dark";
      }
    }
    if (saved_theme == "dark") {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "dark");
    } else {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-theme", "light");
    }

    const tocDisplay = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_toc_display');
    if (tocDisplay) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-toc-display", tocDisplay);
    }
    const readingMode = localStorage.getItem('arxiv_html_paper_reading_mode');
    if (readingMode) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-reading-mode", readingMode);
    }
    // Pre-apply spinout-banner dismissal here, before the banner paints, so it
    // never flashes in only to be hidden later by the deferred arxiv-header.js.
    // Key matches arxiv-header.js: "arxiv-banner-dismissed:" + data-banner-name.
    if (localStorage.getItem('arxiv-banner-dismissed:spinout-nonprofit')) {
      document.documentElement.setAttribute("data-banner-dismissed", "");
    }
  }
  // Run as soon as JS starts, to minimize repainting
  initializeReadingPreferences();
</script>

<article class="ltx_document ltx_authors_1line">
<h1 class="ltx_title ltx_title_document">Semantic Substrate Theory:
<br class="ltx_break">An Operator-Theoretic Framework for Geometric Semantic Drift</h1>
<div class="ltx_authors">
<span class="ltx_creator ltx_role_author">
<span class="ltx_personname">Stephen Russell
</span><span class="ltx_author_notes"><span class="ltx_author_notes_content">
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>Intelligent Systems and Robotics Department
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_affiliation"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Affiliation: </span>University of West Florida
</span>
<span class="ltx_contact ltx_role_email"><span class="ltx_contact_name">Email: </span><a href="mailto:"><span id="id1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_typewriter">russell@uwf.edu</span></a>
</span></span></span></span></div>

<div id="abstract1" class="ltx_abstract"><h6 class="ltx_title ltx_title_abstract">Abstract</h6>
    
<p id="abstract1.1" class="ltx_p">Most semantic drift studies report multiple signals e.g., embedding displacement, neighbor changes, distributional divergence, and recursive trajectory instability, without a shared explanatory theory that relates them. This paper proposes a formalization of these signals in one time-indexed substrate, <math id="abstract1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}=(X,d_{t},P_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}=(X,d_{t},P_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>, combining embedding geometry with local diffusion. Within this substrate, node-level neighborhood drift measures changes in local conditional distributions, coarse Ricci curvature measures local contractivity of semantic diffusion, and recursive drift probes stability of iterated semantic operators. This manuscript specifies the formal model, assumptions, and tests that can refute the model. Herein, the paper introduces bridge mass, a node-level aggregate of incident negative curvature, as a predictor of future neighborhood rewiring. This paper provides the theory and test contracts; empirical performance is deferred to subsequent studies.</p>
  
</div>
<section id="S1" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">1 </span>Introduction</h2>

<div id="S1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Semantic drift is usually treated as a detection problem: something changed, therefore an alert should be raised. In practice that orientation is operationally useful, but weak on explanation. The same drift-score can reflect very different generative regimes: benign local churn inside a stable semantic basin, boundary crossing between basins, or instability induced by an iterative transformation process. Without an explicit mechanistic account, detection is harder to trust, debug, and govern. A separate problem is structural fragmentation. Approaches targeting semantics track different quantities and label all of them “drift.” Results then become hard to compare, and interpretation itself drifts post hoc.</p>
</div>
<div id="S1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">As the metrics themselves are fundamentally robust in what they respectively measure, the goal should not be to replace the existing metrics. What is needed is unifying theory that places them in one formal construct, so each has a defined role. This paper proposes that theory and calls it the semantic substrate developing the formalism and pre-specified predictions granting room for subsequent empirical evalauation. Accordingly, this manuscript stays at the theory level and states predictions in falsifiable form.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S2" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">2 </span>Positioning in the Literature</h2>

<div id="S2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Diachronic distributional and embedding methods made large-scale semantic change measurable, especially across long historical corpora <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib8" title="" class="ltx_ref">8</a>, <a href="#bib.bib6" title="" class="ltx_ref">6</a>]</cite>. Semantic measurement tasks then improved comparability by standardizing unsupervised lexical-change evaluation protocols <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib1" title="" class="ltx_ref">1</a>, <a href="#bib.bib11" title="" class="ltx_ref">11</a>]</cite>. The same literature also shows that frequency and modeling artifacts can produce apparent “laws,” unless controls are explicit <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib4" title="" class="ltx_ref">4</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p2.1" class="ltx_p">In parallel, coarse Ricci curvature gives an operator-level notion of local contraction for Markov processes on metric spaces <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib9" title="" class="ltx_ref">9</a>, <a href="#bib.bib10" title="" class="ltx_ref">10</a>]</cite>. Graph adaptations connect curvature to local clustering and bottleneck structure, making it usable for neighborhood-level diagnostics <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib7" title="" class="ltx_ref">7</a>]</cite>. Simultaneously, dynamic and contextualized representations are shown to improve temporal resolution, but they still leave mechanism labels loosely coupled to one another <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib2" title="" class="ltx_ref">2</a>, <a href="#bib.bib5" title="" class="ltx_ref">5</a>]</cite>.</p>
</div>
<div id="S2.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S2.p3.1" class="ltx_p">The gap is not metric availability; it is the lack of a shared construct where node drift, edge fragility, and recursive instability are defined in commensurate terms.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S3" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">3 </span>Semantic Substrate</h2>

<div id="Thmdefinition1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefinition1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 1</span></span><span id="Thmdefinition1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Semantic substrate)<span id="Thmdefinition1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefinition1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefinition1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefinition1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For each analysis window <math id="Thmdefinition1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, the semantic substrate as is defined as <math id="Thmdefinition1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="S_{t}=(X,d_{t},P_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>S</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>X</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">S_{t}=(X,d_{t},P_{t})</annotation></semantics></math>. Here <math id="Thmdefinition1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math> is a set of semantic objects, <math id="Thmdefinition1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is an embedding-induced metric on <math id="Thmdefinition1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="Thmdefinition1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is a one-step Markov diffusion kernel.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><math id="S3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is instantiated through an embedding map <math id="S3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="f_{t}:X\to\mathbb{R}^{d}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>f</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.278em" rspace="0.278em">:</mo><mrow><mi>X</mi><mo stretchy="false">→</mo><msup><mi>ℝ</mi><mi>d</mi></msup></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">f_{t}:X\to\mathbb{R}^{d}</annotation></semantics></math>, then build a neighborhood graph <math id="S3.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}=(V,E_{t})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>V</mi><mo>,</mo><msub><mi>E</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}=(V,E_{t})</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="S3.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="V=X" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>V</mi><mo>=</mo><mi>X</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">V=X</annotation></semantics></math> (e.g., kNN or mutual-kNN). For each node <math id="S3.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>, define the local neighborhood measure <math id="S3.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{x}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{x}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>
</div>
<div id="S3.p2" class="ltx_para">
<table id="S3.E1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S3.E1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{x}^{(t)}(z)=\begin{cases}\alpha,&amp;z=x,\\

</table>
<p id="S3.p2.1" class="ltx_p">with idleness <math id="S3.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha\in[0,1]" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>α</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">[</mo><mrow><mn>0</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">]</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha\in[0,1]</annotation></semantics></math> and edge weights <math id="S3.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="w_{xz}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>w</mi><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>z</mi></mrow></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">w_{xz}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>. Then set</p>
<table id="S3.Ex1" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

</table>
</div>
<div id="S3.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S3.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Operationally, drift occurs when geometry (<math id="S3.p3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>), diffusion (<math id="S3.p3.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="P_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">P_{t}</annotation></semantics></math>), or both evolve across windows.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">4 </span>Four Drift Modes as Observables of One Substrate</h2>

<div id="S4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The semantic substrate decomposes drift into four non-equivalent modes.</p>
</div>
<section id="S4.SS1" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.1 </span>Translational drift</h3>

<div id="S4.SS1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A direct displacement observable is</p>
<table id="S4.E2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">

</table>
<p id="S4.SS1.p1.2" class="ltx_p">with cosine-based analogs as alternatives. This captures motion in embedding space, but is vulnerable to global embedding reconfiguration and alignment effects.</p>
</div>
</section>

<div id="S4.SS2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Define neighborhood-distribution shift at node <math id="S4.SS2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>:</p>

<p id="S4.SS2.p1.3" class="ltx_p">These quantities measure local semantic neighborhood redistribution rather than global translation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS3" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.3 </span>Dynamical drift</h3>

<div id="S4.SS3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Let an iterative semantic operator be given by</p>
<table id="S4.E5" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.E5.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x_{k+1}=F(x_{k})," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>x</mi><mrow><mi>k</mi><mo>+</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>F</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><msub><mi>x</mi><mi>k</mi></msub><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x_{k+1}=F(x_{k}),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(5)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS3.p1.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> can represent recursive rewriting, summarization, or transformation followed by projection into <math id="S4.SS3.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>. In this regime, drift is a trajectory property (sensitivity, basin switching, persistence), not only a two-window difference.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S4.SS4" class="ltx_subsection">
<h3 class="ltx_title ltx_title_subsection"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_subsection">4.4 </span>Process drift (composition of evolution and intervention)</h3>

<div id="S4.SS4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Observed drift in deployed systems is often generated by semantic evolution and pipeline interventions. Let <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote organic semantic evolution (for example, corpus shift or endogenous updates), and let <math id="S4.SS4.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> denote intervention (for example, retrieval grounding, policy filtering, safety tuning, or decoding constraints). Define the composed update operator</p>
<table id="S4.Ex2" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="H_{t}=G_{t}\circ F_{t}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>H</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">H_{t}=G_{t}\circ F_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Process drift is the change introduced by this composition beyond either factor in isolation. Operationally, this separates “what semantics would have done” from “what the pipeline made them do.”</p>
</div>
<div id="S4.SS4.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.1" class="ltx_p">This decomposition also implies order effects when intervention and evolution do not commute:</p>
<table id="S4.Ex3" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S4.Ex3.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}\circ F_{t}\neq F_{t}\circ G_{t}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>≠</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.222em">∘</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}\circ F_{t}\neq F_{t}\circ G_{t}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S4.SS4.p2.2" class="ltx_p">Applying an intervention a priori, versus after, semantic evolution can therefore produce different neighborhoods, curvature profiles, and rewiring risk even when the same components are used.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S5" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">5 </span>Curvature and Structural Fragility</h2>

<div id="Thmdefinition2" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_definition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmdefinition2.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Definition 2</span></span><span id="Thmdefinition2.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Coarse Ricci curvature)<span id="Thmdefinition2.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmdefinition2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmdefinition2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmdefinition2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">For <math id="Thmdefinition2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x\neq y" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x\neq y</annotation></semantics></math> with <math id="Thmdefinition2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}(x,y)&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}(x,y)&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, define</span></p>
<table id="S5.E6" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E6.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{\mathrm{OR}}^{(t)}(x,y)=1-\frac{\mathsf{W}_{1}\!\left(m_{x}^{(t)},m_{y}^{(t)}\right)}{d_{t}(x,y)}." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>κ</mi><mi>OR</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><mfrac><mrow><msub><mi>𝖶</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>,</mo><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>y</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow><mrow><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mfrac></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{\mathrm{OR}}^{(t)}(x,y)=1-\frac{\mathsf{W}_{1}\!\left(m_{x}^{(t)},m_{y}^{(t)}\right)}{d_{t}(x,y)}.</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(6)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Positive curvature corresponds to locally contractive one-step diffusion and negative curvature corresponds to locally expansive, bridge-like structure.</p>
</div>
<div id="Thmproposition1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_proposition">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmproposition1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Proposition 1</span></span><span id="Thmproposition1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold"> </span>(Imported contractivity result)<span id="Thmproposition1.4" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmproposition1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmproposition1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Let <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}=\inf_{x\neq y}\kappa_{\mathrm{OR}}^{(t)}(x,y)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo rspace="0.1389em">=</mo><mrow><msub><mo lspace="0.1389em" rspace="0.167em">inf</mo><mrow><mi>x</mi><mo>≠</mo><mi>y</mi></mrow></msub><mrow><msubsup><mi>κ</mi><mi>OR</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}=\inf_{x\neq y}\kappa_{\mathrm{OR}}^{(t)}(x,y)</annotation></semantics></math>. If <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa_{0}&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa_{0}&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>, then for all probability measures <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mu,\nu" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mu,\nu</annotation></semantics></math> on <math id="Thmproposition1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathcal{X}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi class="ltx_font_mathcaligraphic">𝒳</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathcal{X}</annotation></semantics></math>,</span></p>
<table id="S5.E7" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E7.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu P_{t},\nu P_{t})\leq(1-\kappa_{0})\,\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu,\nu)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝖶</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝖶</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu P_{t},\nu P_{t})\leq(1-\kappa_{0})\,\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu,\nu).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(7)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="Thmproposition1.p1.2" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmproposition1.p1.2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Consequently,</span></p>
<table id="S5.E8" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E8.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu P_{t}^{k},\nu P_{t}^{k})\leq(1-\kappa_{0})^{k}\,\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu,\nu)." display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>𝖶</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mi>μ</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>ν</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msubsup><mi>P</mi><mi>t</mi><mi>k</mi></msubsup></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≤</mo><mrow><msup><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>−</mo><msub><mi>κ</mi><mn>0</mn></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mi>k</mi></msup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mi>𝖶</mi><mn>1</mn></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo lspace="0em">.</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu P_{t}^{k},\nu P_{t}^{k})\leq(1-\kappa_{0})^{k}\,\mathsf{W}_{1}(\mu,\nu).</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(8)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
</div>
</div>
<div id="Thmremark1" class="ltx_theorem ltx_theorem_remark">
<h6 class="ltx_title ltx_runin ltx_title_theorem"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_theorem"><span id="Thmremark1.2" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Remark 1</span></span><span id="Thmremark1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">.</span></h6>
<div id="Thmremark1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="Thmremark1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="Thmremark1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_italic">Equation (<a href="#S5.E7" title="In Proposition 1 (Imported contractivity result). ‣ 5 Curvature and Structural Fragility ‣ Semantic Substrate Theory:An Operator-Theoretic Framework for Geometric Semantic Drift" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">7</span></a>) provides an operator-level stability condition that complements node-level drift magnitudes.</span></p>
</div>
</div>
<div id="S5.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p2.1" class="ltx_p">Define node-level bridge mass:</p>
<table id="S5.E9" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S5.E9.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}(x)=\sum_{y\in N_{t}(x)}\pi_{t}(x,y)\,\bigl(-\kappa_{\mathrm{OR}}^{(t)}(x,y)\bigr)_{+}," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo rspace="0.111em">=</mo><mrow><munder><mo movablelimits="false">∑</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0.170em" rspace="0em">​</mo><msub><mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">(</mo><mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><msubsup><mi>κ</mi><mi>OR</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo maxsize="1.200em" minsize="1.200em">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}(x)=\sum_{y\in N_{t}(x)}\pi_{t}(x,y)\,\bigl(-\kappa_{\mathrm{OR}}^{(t)}(x,y)\bigr)_{+},</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(9)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S5.p2.2" class="ltx_p">where <math id="S5.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(u)_{+}=\max(u,0)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo>+</mo></msub><mo>=</mo><mrow><mi>max</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>u</mi><mo>,</mo><mn>0</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(u)_{+}=\max(u,0)</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S5.p2.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\pi_{t}(x,y)\geq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>≥</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\pi_{t}(x,y)\geq 0</annotation></semantics></math>, and <math id="S5.p2.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\sum_{y\in N_{t}(x)}\pi_{t}(x,y)=1" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><msub><mo>∑</mo><mrow><mi>y</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><msub><mi>N</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></msub><mrow><msub><mi>π</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>y</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mn>1</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\sum_{y\in N_{t}(x)}\pi_{t}(x,y)=1</annotation></semantics></math>.
Large <math id="S5.p2.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> indicates that a substantial share of incident neighborhood structure lay in the (bridge-like) regime.</p>
</div>
<figure id="S5.F1" class="ltx_figure"><img src="2602.18699v1/images/substrate_example.png" id="S5.F1.g1" class="ltx_graphics ltx_centering ltx_img_square" style="aspect-ratio:381/315;" width="381" height="315" alt="Refer to caption">
<figcaption class="ltx_caption ltx_centering"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_figure">Figure 1: </span><span id="S5.F1.3" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Semantic basins and bridges in substrate geometry.</span>
Blue wells depict positively curved basin regions (<math id="S5.F1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa&gt;0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>&gt;</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa&gt;0</annotation></semantics></math>) where local diffusion tends to be contractive and trajectories are pulled toward stable neighborhoods. The green ridge indicates a negatively curved bridge regime (<math id="S5.F1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\kappa\leq 0" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>κ</mi><mo>≤</mo><mn>0</mn></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\kappa\leq 0</annotation></semantics></math>), where diffusion is locally expansive and connectivity is fragile. Nodes near or traversing bridge structure are more susceptible to neighborhood rewiring under perturbation or intervention.</figcaption>
</figure>
<div id="S5.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S5.p3.1" class="ltx_p">Figure <a href="#S5.F1" title="Figure 1 ‣ 5 Curvature and Structural Fragility ‣ Semantic Substrate Theory:An Operator-Theoretic Framework for Geometric Semantic Drift" class="ltx_ref"><span class="ltx_text ltx_ref_tag">1</span></a> provides a visual intuition aid: positively curved basin regions are locally self-reinforcing, while negatively curved bridge regions are more susceptible to rewiring under perturbation.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S6" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">6 </span>Assumptions</h2>

<div id="S6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The theory depends on six assumptions that can be violated.</p>
</div>
<div id="S6.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S6.I1" class="ltx_enumerate" style="--ltx-enum-leftmargin:2.2em;">
<li id="S6.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S6.I1.i1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A1:</span></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Local geometric validity:</span> The metric <math id="S6.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="d_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>d</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">d_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> is locally meaningful for the domain, even if global geometry is imperfect.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S6.I1.i2.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A2:</span></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Neighborhood as conditional proxy:</span> The measure <math id="S6.I1.i2.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="m_{x}^{(t)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>m</mi><mi>x</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">m_{x}^{(t)}</annotation></semantics></math> is an adequate approximation to local contextual meaning around <math id="S6.I1.i2.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math>.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S6.I1.i3.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A3:</span></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Within-window stationarity.</span> The substrate is approximately stationary inside each analysis window.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S6.I1.i4.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A4:</span></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Confound control:</span> Frequency, utilization, and sampling effects are controlled or modeled explicitly.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S6.I1.i5.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A5:</span></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Graph robustness:</span> Qualitative conclusions persist under reasonable variation of <math id="S6.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="k" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>k</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">k</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S6.I1.i5.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\alpha" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>α</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\alpha</annotation></semantics></math>, and weighting rules.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S6.I1.i6" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item"><span id="S6.I1.i6.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">A6:</span></span> 
<div id="S6.I1.i6.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S6.I1.i6.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S6.I1.i6.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Operator relevance:</span> For recursive studies, the chosen <math id="S6.I1.i6.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>F</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F</annotation></semantics></math> approximates an operational transformation of interest.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">7 </span>Testable Predictions and Falsification Criteria</h2>

<div id="S7.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.p1.1" class="ltx_p">We evaluate the theory through pre-specified predictions.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S7.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S7.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">P1.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Bridge mass as a leading indicator:</span> Bridge mass <math id="S7.I1.i1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="B_{t}(x)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>B</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">B_{t}(x)</annotation></semantics></math> predicts out-of-sample rewiring drift <math id="S7.I1.i1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\mathrm{rw}}(x;t,t+\Delta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>rw</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\mathrm{rw}}(x;t,t+\Delta)</annotation></semantics></math> after adjustment for frequency and sampling controls.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">P2.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Boundary concentration:</span> Large rewiring events are concentrated in nodes whose incident curvature shifts toward the negative regime.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">P3.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Intervention directionality:</span> Stabilizing interventions increase local contractivity and reduce future rewiring risk; destabilizing interventions show the opposite pattern.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">P4.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Dynamics-geometry alignment:</span> Recursive trajectories that traverse negative-curvature regions have higher basin-switch rates and longer perturbation persistence.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S7.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">P5.</span> 
<div id="S7.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S7.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Non-commutativity effect:</span> Intervention order is not neutral. They are defines thusly,</p>
<table id="S7.Ex4" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S7.Ex4.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{comm}}(x,t)=d\!\left((G_{t}\!\circ\!F_{t})(x),(F_{t}\!\circ\!G_{t})(x)\right)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>comm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mpadded style="width:0.350em;" width="0.350em"><mi>d</mi></mpadded><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo>(</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.052em">∘</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo><mrow><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.222em" rspace="0.052em">∘</mo><msub><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{comm}}(x,t)=d\!\left((G_{t}\!\circ\!F_{t})(x),(F_{t}\!\circ\!G_{t})(x)\right),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S7.I1.i5.p1.2" class="ltx_p">Larger <math id="S7.I1.i5.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{comm}}(x,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>comm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{comm}}(x,t)</annotation></semantics></math> should be associated with larger differences in endpoint stability and rewiring risk across intervention timing schedules.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Minimal operationalization of P5.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Fix two intervention families <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}^{(1)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>1</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}^{(1)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}^{(2)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mn>2</mn><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}^{(2)}</annotation></semantics></math> and one evolution family <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m3" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> before inspecting outcomes.
For each node <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m4" class="ltx_Math" alttext="x" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>x</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">x</annotation></semantics></math> and window <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m5" class="ltx_Math" alttext="t" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>t</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">t</annotation></semantics></math>, evaluate matched schedules <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m6" class="ltx_Math" alttext="G_{t}^{(i)}\!\circ\!F_{t}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup><mo lspace="0.052em" rspace="0.052em">∘</mo><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">G_{t}^{(i)}\!\circ\!F_{t}</annotation></semantics></math> and <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m7" class="ltx_Math" alttext="F_{t}\!\circ\!G_{t}^{(i)}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>F</mi><mi>t</mi></msub><mo lspace="0.052em" rspace="0.052em">∘</mo><msubsup><mi>G</mi><mi>t</mi><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>i</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></msubsup></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">F_{t}\!\circ\!G_{t}^{(i)}</annotation></semantics></math>, <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m8" class="ltx_Math" alttext="i\in\{1,2\}" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mi>i</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">{</mo><mrow><mn>1</mn><mo>,</mo><mn>2</mn></mrow><mo stretchy="false">}</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">i\in\{1,2\}</annotation></semantics></math>, under identical budgets and confound controls.
Endpoints pre-specified before outcome inspection:
(i) future rewiring drift <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p1.m9" class="ltx_Math" alttext="D_{\mathrm{rw}}(x;t,t+\Delta)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi>D</mi><mi>rw</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo>,</mo><mrow><mi>t</mi><mo>+</mo><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">D_{\mathrm{rw}}(x;t,t+\Delta)</annotation></semantics></math>,
(ii) basin-switch rate under recursive probing,
(iii) calibration error of rewiring-risk forecasts.</p>
</div>
<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.1" class="ltx_p">The strict null is order neutrality: after controls, <math id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px1.p2.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\Delta_{\mathrm{comm}}(x,t)" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><msub><mi mathvariant="normal">Δ</mi><mi>comm</mi></msub><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>x</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>t</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\Delta_{\mathrm{comm}}(x,t)</annotation></semantics></math> adds no incremental predictive value beyond baseline drift and frequency covariates.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2" class="ltx_paragraph">
<h4 class="ltx_title ltx_title_paragraph">Falsification rule.</h4>

<div id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S7.SS0.SSS0.Px2.p1.1" class="ltx_p">A prediction is rejected if it does not improve out-of-sample discrimination or calibration relative to controls and simpler baselines.</p>
</div>
</section>
</section>
<section id="S8" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">8 </span>Protocol for Empirical Validation</h2>

<div id="S8.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Although this manuscript is theory-only, an evaluation protocol is provided to limit hindsight bias in subsequent empirical studies.</p>
</div>
<div id="S8.p2" class="ltx_para">
<ol id="S8.I1" class="ltx_enumerate">
<li id="S8.I1.i1" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">1.</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i1.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i1.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i1.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Define primary endpoints before fitting:</span>
Rank-based discrimination for future rewiring events, calibration error, and sensitivity to window definitions.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I1.i2" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">2.</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i2.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i2.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Specify confound-control procedures in advance:</span>
Frequency matching, placebo windows, and bootstrap/permutation procedures.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I1.i3" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">3.</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i3.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i3.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Report robustness as surfaces, not points:</span>
Vary graph construction choices <math id="S8.I1.i3.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="(k,\alpha,\text{weighting})" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>k</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>α</mi><mo>,</mo><mtext>weighting</mtext><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">(k,\alpha,\text{weighting})</annotation></semantics></math> and report performance/stability over the resulting grid rather than a single tuned setting.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I1.i4" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">4.</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i4.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i4.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i4.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Keep drift channels separate in reporting:</span>
Tabulate translational drift and rewiring drift separately in every main results table.</p>
</div></li>
<li id="S8.I1.i5" class="ltx_item" style="list-style-type:none;"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_item">5.</span> 
<div id="S8.I1.i5.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.I1.i5.p1.1" class="ltx_p"><span id="S8.I1.i5.p1.1.1" class="ltx_text ltx_font_bold">Commit recursive settings before scoring:</span>
For recursive experiments, commit to operator families and perturbation schemes prior to outcome inspection.</p>
</div></li>
</ol>
</div>
<div id="S8.p3" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S8.p3.1" class="ltx_p">For added transparency, future empirical work can document and justify deviations from this protocol. Together, these constraints reduce hindsight bias and help keep theoretical claims aligned with empirical evidence.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S9" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">9 </span>Computational Considerations</h2>

<div id="S9.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S9.p1.1" class="ltx_p">Exact optimal transport can be expensive when computed across many local comparisons. Entropic regularization yields the Sinkhorn objective</p>
<table id="S9.E10" class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_table">

<tbody><tr class="ltx_equation ltx_eqn_row ltx_align_baseline">
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padleft"></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_align_center"><math id="S9.E10.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\mathsf{W}_{1}^{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)=\min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\langle C,\gamma\rangle-\varepsilon H(\gamma)," display="block" intent=":literal"><semantics><mrow><mrow><mrow><msubsup><mi>𝖶</mi><mn>1</mn><mi>ε</mi></msubsup><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>=</mo><mrow><mrow><munder><mi>min</mi><mrow><mi>γ</mi><mo>∈</mo><mrow><mi mathvariant="normal">Π</mi><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>μ</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>ν</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></munder><mo>⁡</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟨</mo><mrow><mi>C</mi><mo>,</mo><mi>γ</mi></mrow><mo stretchy="false">⟩</mo></mrow></mrow><mo>−</mo><mrow><mi>ε</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mi>H</mi><mo lspace="0em" rspace="0em">​</mo><mrow><mo stretchy="false">(</mo><mi>γ</mi><mo stretchy="false">)</mo></mrow></mrow></mrow></mrow><mo>,</mo></mrow><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\mathsf{W}_{1}^{\varepsilon}(\mu,\nu)=\min_{\gamma\in\Pi(\mu,\nu)}\langle C,\gamma\rangle-\varepsilon H(\gamma),</annotation></semantics></math></td>
<td class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_center_padright"></td>
<td rowspan="1" class="ltx_eqn_cell ltx_eqn_eqno ltx_align_middle ltx_align_right"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_equation ltx_align_right">(10)</span></td></tr></tbody>
</table>
<p id="S9.p1.2" class="ltx_p">which is solved via matrix-scaling iterations and is typically far cheaper in practice than exact linear programming <cite class="ltx_cite ltx_citemacro_cite">[<a href="#bib.bib3" title="" class="ltx_ref">3</a>]</cite>. Empirical reports can specify <math id="S9.p1.m1" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math>, the iteration budget, stopping tolerance, and wall-clock runtime. Approximation error can be assessed as a function of <math id="S9.p1.m2" class="ltx_Math" alttext="\varepsilon" display="inline" intent=":literal"><semantics><mi>ε</mi><annotation encoding="application/x-tex">\varepsilon</annotation></semantics></math> and compute budget; where feasible, a subset of instances can be cross-validated against exact OT to quantify bias.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S10" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">10 </span>Limitations</h2>

<div id="S10.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S10.p1.1" class="ltx_p">The substrate does not eliminate the need for careful data design. Drift estimates can be distorted by embedding pathologies, unstable graph construction, or mis-specified windowing. Strong anisotropy or poor semantic alignment can make the induced geometry uninformative. If neighborhood graphs are unstable, rewiring and curvature summaries may primarily reflect construction noise rather than semantic change. Mis-specified window boundaries can also alias short-term variability into apparent structural drift. Finally, curvature is a mechanistic variable rather than a complete explanation: claims should rest on incremental predictive value relative to confound controls and competing drift signals.</p>
</div>
</section>
<section id="S11" class="ltx_section">
<h2 class="ltx_title ltx_title_section"><span class="ltx_tag ltx_tag_section">11 </span>Conclusion</h2>

<div id="S11.p1" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.p1.1" class="ltx_p">This work formulates semantic drift on a single evolving substrate that renders translational movement, neighborhood rewiring, recursive instability, and intervention-order effects comparable within one operator–geometric model. A core theoretical contribution is a decomposition: multiple drift “signals” are treated as coupled measurements (projections) of a shared latent evolution, enabling mechanistic distinctions, e.g., within-basin churn versus basin transitions versus recursion-induced instability, that are not recoverable from detection-only scores. This perspective also clarifies major failure modes (embedding anisotropy, graph instability, window aliasing), improves interpretability, and supports more trustworthy debugging and governance of drift pipelines.</p>
</div>
<div id="S11.p2" class="ltx_para">
<p id="S11.p2.1" class="ltx_p">To keep these theoretical commitments empirically accountable, a test contract: explicit assumptions, operational predictions, and rejection criteria that define an empirical program are provided. The framework is therefore intended to be evaluated by out-of-sample discrimination and calibration under confound controls and robustness analysis, rather than by conceptual appeal alone.</p>
</div>
</section>
